public_rationale: OpenAI described broad categories of training material without substantially identifying the underlying sources. The contemporary DALL-E 3 system card supports Marcus's ordinary claim of limited transparency. It also limits that conclusion: OpenAI did disclose some information about its data and filtering.
limitations: Transparency has no numerical threshold in the claim.
This finding concerns substantive source disclosure for the models discussed, not every OpenAI model.
The system-card availability date refers to the original publication, not the undated reproduction.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has not been transparent about its training data.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI, despite its name, has not been transparent about what it has been trained on.
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

from_speaker: what it has been trained on
our_interpretation: Transparency means identifying substantive training sources sufficiently for outsiders to understand what material was used. It does not require publishing every training example.
The claim concerns OpenAI's then-current generative models, particularly GPT-4 and DALL-E 3.
For this ongoing state, the reporting window is the latest calendar quarter through the post: October 1–December 29, 2023. Earlier documentation is context.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary documentation supplies broad training-data categories while withholding substantive information identifying the underlying sources.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary public disclosures substantially identify the training sources for the models discussed.
